keys.explanation: Change errors, incomplete procedures, and weak maintenance discipline are organizational contributors to downtime; a feeder short, lightning strike, or isolated UPS component is a technical or environmental event rather than this organizational category.
Plenums and ceiling spaces can bypass door controls unless secured or monitored; a propped door, network-only view, or access-system assumption does not secure the vertical path.

Low-residue agents can suit electronics when correctly selected and used, but CO2 has oxygen-displacement hazards; corrosive powder, replacing building suppression, and untrained use are not equivalent benefits. The current NFPA 10 catalog supports the trained-use boundary.

Remove a vendor from the authorized-access list when the contract need ends; a signed contract is not a continuing badge authorization, and a shared visitor account or quarterly review leaves least privilege stale. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 PE-2 supports the control.

Hot work adds ignition near cables, packaging, and dust, so authorization, controls, extinguishing equipment, and fire watch matter; sparks do not polish fiber, a supervisor alone does not waive permits, and smoke is not harmless to detection. The current eCFR supports this control boundary.

Strong power-frequency magnetic fields come from high current, so transformers, busbars and UPS plant are the sources worth mapping. The other options fail the same test from different directions: plastic panels and fibre carry no current at all, exit signage draws milliamps, and an empty tray is only a source when something energised is lying in it.

International standards provide broadly usable technical alignment that countries and projects may adopt or reference differently; they do not replace national codes, ban standards bodies, or turn marketing into design criteria.

Article 700 emergency lighting needs its own verified emergency source and branch-circuit path; IT UPS ride-through does not prove compliance, and neither a rack UPS nor a generator for every luminaire is automatic.
Li-ion offers density and lifecycle trade-offs, but still needs battery management, monitoring, and fire design; it does not create 2N automatically or remove thermal concerns.
Exit signs identify the egress route; they are not fire-alarm notification appliances or a replacement for route markings, and they do not provide detailed task lighting.

Blanking panels and brush strips seal leakage paths that would otherwise let supply air bypass equipment or exhaust recirculate to intakes, so they affect air-cooled inlet temperature rather than serving as trim, promoting mixing, or applying only to liquid racks.
Direct-to-chip cooling brings liquid through cold plates or loops to high-heat components; it is not room-air-only, a grounding replacement, or merely hot-aisle containment.
Single-mode provides longer-reach and bandwidth headroom for backbones; deliberate modal dispersion, forbidden connectors, and sub-metre-only assumptions are not selection goals.

The single point of failure is a component or path whose lone failure can interrupt the protected load; a sensor, a dual-path system with inadequate capacity, or a redundant UPS string is not automatically such a point.
Pre-terminated trunks speed installation with factory-controlled fit and terminations; they do not remove polarity planning, pathway design, or acceptance testing.

Basin level and makeup flow are a water balance: an unexplained rise in makeup means loss somewhere -- a leak, excessive blowdown, or a supply problem -- and it shows up before thermal performance degrades. It does not replace rack-inlet sensing, though: it is an upstream plant signal, and inferring hall conditions from it would miss anything downstream of the loop.

Zero-U means the PDU mounts in the vertical rear or side channel, consuming none of the horizontal U that IT equipment needs -- which is the whole point of the form factor and why 800 mm cabinets are chosen for dense power. A horizontal shelf, plant-side enclosure, or return-air plenum is a different installation, not the rack's vertical zero-U channel.

The checklist has to include the supervisory points for fire and security AND the health of the monitoring itself, because a dead sensor and a silent collector both read as calm. Monitoring the monitors is the part most often missed. The other options are business and cosmetic metrics with no operational state behind them.
Recirculation is hot exhaust returning to intakes instead of a clean return; cold supply short-circuiting is bypass, while liquid loops and stationary air are different cases.
UPS ride-through carries IT through genset start and transfer; the fire system does not become the power path, and an unprotected load would not simply wait through a multi-hour start.
Containment integrity matters because doors, blanks, and seals prevent leakage and mixing; gaps do not improve separation, battery autonomy, or CRAH redundancy.
Concentrated load is a heavy force applied through a small contact area such as equipment feet; aisle paint, room-average kW, and DNS selection do not test panel or pedestal loading.
DCIM ties inventory, power capacity, and change workflows to facilities data—not just environment sensing; fire release, transfer-switch control, and protection relaying remain distinct functions.
The guideline recommends practice and becomes binding only through code, contract, or policy adoption; it does not automatically override the AHJ or carry criminal penalties by itself.

The EPA case is useful precisely because its closed-loop reuse system still required makeup water and site-specific rights and permits. DOE FEMP and the NREL ESIF report distinguish recirculating liquid paths and dry or evaporative heat rejection, but neither grants a universal siting permission. ISO/IEC 30134-9:2022 supplies the WUE KPI and measurement categories; it does not turn a project example into a benchmark or permit.

TIA-942-B §1.2 defines requirements but does not mandate or provide an assessment program. 'Designed to TIA-942-B Rated-3' is a self-declaration by the designer or owner — it may or may not have been verified by a third party. A due-diligence reviewer should ask whether an independent assessor validated the claim and, if so, request the assessment report. Self-declaration and third-party assessment are distinct; the marketing phrase does not prove either.
Restricted-zone visitors need identity checks, temporary credentials, escort, and sign-in/out; permanent unrestricted or shared badges destroy zone control and audit.

The campus can have diverse carriers and adequate loading yet fail if easements, deed restrictions, or landlord rules block fuel or antenna rights; utility access alone does not remove those legal constraints.
Uniform, concentrated, and rolling ratings describe area, point, and wheeled-equipment forces respectively; they are not identical aesthetic categories or merely cable weight.
Distance and layout are the strongest cheap tools for power-frequency magnetic fields; RF paint, removing bonding, or changing phase supply are different or unsafe responses.

Logos are not laterals. A shared duct bank or manhole collapses both providers to one backhoe cut. That is the building oral. It is not the east-west fabric: a single-path IB/RoCE mesh remains one training job even if the laterals were actually diverse. Do not invent a reach metre.
Security theatre is impressive visible control while roofs, yards, or processes remain weak; integrated anti-passback, CCTV, and LOTO are real layers rather than theatre.

A job-based IDP with competency goals is the grounded manager artifact: the current public OPM career-development guidance describes IDPs as records of career goals, development objectives, and training opportunities such as rotational assignments, and ties them to learning objectives and competencies. This is a curriculum grounding receipt, not a credential or certification claim.
Actionable alerts beat naked point names during incidents; runbook links guide the next action without eliminating calibration or turning every log entry into an executive page.

The UK Department for Education's Service Management standard, Version 1, identifies user satisfaction through a single point of entry into service support. The item applies that specific public statement to the CDFOS customer-satisfaction heading; it does not prescribe a particular portal or satisfaction score.

Loss of cooling can raise inlet temperature until servers throttle or trip, cascading into application loss while power remains available; a healthy blanking panel, clean UPS transfer, or dual live source is not a cascade.

Unsealed penetrations defeat rated barriers and let smoke or fire spread; openings do not improve suppression, and supervision or visual preference cannot waive firestopping. The current NFPA 1 preview supports the code-governed compartmentation boundary.
Without test records, failed lamps or batteries may remain hidden until an outage; codes and manufacturers generally require functional testing, not prohibit it.

30134-6 is ERF (Energy Reuse Factor). ERE is not that part. The series has more than three letters; this course names the distinction and stops. No single PUE target as law. Sustainability-track depth is not this leftover.
Offline or standby leaves the load on utility until a failure forces transfer—cheap but not preferred for critical core IT; it is not universal, notch-free, or battery-free.

policy: e2e/harness and post-grade explanations only; not the learner exam payload
